articles.title: Guide to Following the 2026-27 NBA: Western Conference
articles.standfirst: Rosters, moves, starting fives and preview of the 15 teams in the Western Conference
articles.summary: Rosters, moves, starting fives and preview of the 15 teams in the Western Conference
articles.body:
Unless teams like the Nuggets , the Wolves , the Rockets , or, to a lesser extent, the Lakers , raise some doubts, everything seems to indicate that the Western Conference is heading toward a new final between the Spurs and the Thunder.

And in that battle, the Texans start with an advantage, having strengthened their extraordinary roster—the one that played in the NBA Finals —with Tobias Harris , while Oklahoma continue searching for the balance between saving money and competitiveness. For San Antonio , the Finals arrived ahead of schedule, but 2027 could already be their moment. Their leader, Victor Wembanyama , could even become the fifth non-American player to win the MVP consecutively.

Although there were some changes to the roster, with the departure of Klay Thompson and the arrival of Santi Aldama, the biggest developments for the Mavs came in the front office. The acquisition of Masai Ujiri gives the team the architect of the Toronto Raptors ' 2019 title. And his first decision was to part ways with Jason Kidd and bring in a breath of fresh air in Dusty May, former coach of the NCAA champion Michigan Wolverines . This year's Mavs will have a strong Spanish presence with Santi Aldama , a veteran expected to make an immediate impact, as is Marcus Sasser , and with Sergio de Larrea , who could see plenty of time on the court. The season will depend on how well Kyrie Irving has recovered.

Renewals: Moussa Cissé (two years) and Naji Marshall (three years).

Additions: Santi Aldama (traded from the Grizzlies), Tarik Biberović (two years), Zaccharie Risacher and Marcus Sasser (traded from the Pistons).

Departures: Marvin Bagley III (free agent to the Nuggets), AJ Johnson (traded to the Grizzlies), Khris Middleton (traded to the Wizards), Ryan Nembhard, Klay Thompson (free agent to the Heat) and Brandon Williams (free agent to the Warriors).

Roster: Santi Aldama, Tarik Biberovic, Max Christie, Moussa Cisse, Sergio de Larrea, Cooper Flagg, Daniel Gafford, Jett Howard, Kyrie Irving, Morez Johnson Jr., Tobi Lawal, Dereck Lively II, Naji Marshall, Caleb Martin, Zaccharie Risacher, Marcus Sasser and P.J. Washington.

Possible starting five: K. Irving, M. Christie, C. Flagg, P. Washington and D. Lively II.

Far from strengthening their roster, the Nuggets ' efforts in the preseason focused on trying to retain Peyton Watson , something they were unable to do. The loss of the promising 24-year-old forward has left a significant gap in an expensive roster and raised concern in the front office about trying to avoid being above the second apron of the salary cap again.

Athletically, another scorer arrives, DeMar DeRozan , who should ease those duties for Jokic and Murray . The pair will continue to be the barometer of a team that aspires to win the championship again (before the Jokic era runs out), despite the initial disadvantage against Thunder and Spurs in the West.

Renewals: Tyus Jones (one year) and Spencer Jones (two years).

Additions: Marvin Bagley III (one year), DeMar DeRozan (one year) and Alpha Diallo (one year).

Departures: Tim Hardaway Jr. (free agent to the Heat) and Peyton Watson (traded to the Cavs).

Roster: Marvin Bagley III, Christian Braun, Trevon Brazile, DeMar DeRozan, Alpha Diallo, Aaron Gordon, DaRon Holmes II, Bryce Hopkins, Cameron Johnson, Nikola Jokic, Spencer Jones, Tyus Jones, Jamal Murray, Ryan Nembhard, Zeke Nnaji, Julian Strawther and Cam Whitmore.

Possible starting five: J. Murray, C. Braun, C. Johnson, A. Gordon and N. Jokic.

The Warriors officially decided to delay the start of any rebuilding process with the contract extension for Stephen Curry . The veteran point guard will continue to be the player the project relies on, helped by other veterans such as Jimmy Butler, Al Horford, Draymond Green, and Kristaps Porzingis . That said, they managed to protect their future Draft picks and will soon have cap space. But as far as the present is concerned, the team will try to improve on last year's 37 wins in an attempt to avoid having to go through the Play-In. Although climbing higher than eighth place may be more than a complicated goal.

Renewals: Charles Bassey (one year), Stephen Curry (two years), Draymond Green (one year), Al Horford (two years), De’Anthony Melton (two years), Gary Payton II (one year), Brandin Podziemski (five years), and Kristaps Porziņģis (two years).

Additions: Georges Niang (one year) and Brandon Williams (one year).

Departures: Quinten Post (free agent to the Grizzlies).

Roster: Charles Bassey, Jimmy Butler III, LJ Cryer, Stephen Curry, Draymond Green, Al Horford, Graham Ike, Yaxel Lendeborg, Malevy Leons, De"Anthony Melton, Moses Moody, Georges Niang, Gary Payton II, Brandin Podziemski, Kristaps Porzingis, Will Richard, Gui Santos and Brandon Williams.

Possible starting five: S. Curry, B. Podziemski, Y. Lendeborg, D. Green and K. Porzingis.

The Rockets have spent two years exiting the League through the back door, which means first-round Playoff elimination. Especially harsh was the one two years ago, when despite having the second-best record in the West, they were eliminated by the seventh seed, Golden State . Out of those two disappointments, a team has grown that could try to join the battle between the Spurs and the Thunder for the conference throne. They re-signed Tari Eason for a little over 80 million and added two veterans to their roster in Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic . They start out on the second tier of favorites in the West .

Extensions: Isaiah Crawford (four years), Tari Eason (five years), Jae’sean Tate (one year) and Amen Thompson (five years).

Additions: Bogdan Bogdanović and Marcus Smart.

Departures: Dorian Finney-Smith and Josh Okogie (free agent to the Jazz).

Roster: Steven Adams, Bogdan Bogdanovic, Clint Capela, Quadir Copeland, Isaiah Crawford, Kevin Durant, Tari Eason, Sean Pedulla, Julian Phillips, Alperen Sengun, Reed Sheppard, Marcus Smart, Jabari Smith Jr., Jae"Sean Tate, Amen Thompson, Bruce Thornton, Oscar Tshiebwe and Fred VanVleet.

Possible starting five: F. VanVleet, A. Thompson, K. Durant, J. Smith Jr. and A. Sengun.

Little by little, the Clippers have changed their landscape until becoming an unrecognizable team. This season they took another step with the trade of Kawhi Leonard to the Raptors. That move kept them very distracted while the cheating committed regarding the salary cap was being investigated. In exchange for Kawhi they get Brandon Ingram , a player as talented as he is disappointing and unreliable, and they acquired Rai Hachimura who may find with the neighboring L.A. the leading role he was asking for with the Lakers . And Bradley Beal remains, who declined a contract extension offer in June to explore the free agent market and ended up re-signing with the Clippers . NBA things.

Renewals: Bradley Beal (two years), Jordan Miller (three years), and Kobe Sanders (four years).

Additions: Johni Broome (traded from the Sixers), Gradey Dick (traded from the Raptors), Rui Hachimura, Brandon Ingram (traded from the Raptors) and Max Strus (traded from the Cavs).

Departures: Bogdan Bogdanović (free agent to the Rockets), John Collins (traded to the Pistons), Kawhi Leonard (traded to the Raptors), and Bennedict Mathurin (Pelicans).

Roster: Bradley Beal, Cam Christie, Gradey Dick, Kris Dunn, Darius Garland, Rui Hachimura, Brandon Ingram, Isaiah Jackson, Derrick Jones Jr., Brook Lopez, Nick Martinelli, Baba Miller, Jordan Miller, Yanic Konan Niederhauser, Jalen Pickett, Kobe Sanders, Max Strus and Keaton Wagler.

Possible starting five: D. Garland, K. Wagler, D. Jones Jr., R. Hachimura and I. Jackson.

In just a couple of days, between when LeBron said he would stay and announced his decision to leave, the Lakers had to change their policy to declare Luka Doncic as the only true superstar. The Slovenian remains as the supreme leader and everything will revolve around him. But the Lakers have been a very active team in the market. They pulled out all the stops to be able to sign a center, Kessler , and they brought in Looney, Mamukelashvili, Sexton, Thybulle and Williams , to try to surround their great leader with good pieces. It will be Year I after LeBron with a new king on the team. Luka has already had one of his wishes fulfilled with the extension of Reaves . The change of ownership with the sale of the team also caused its own distraction during one of the busiest offseasons in franchise history. And at least at the start, the most optimistic see the team fighting for the conference finals.

Renewals: Austin Reaves (four years).

Additions: Quentin Grimes (four years), Jaden Hardy (traded from the Wizards), Walker Kessler (traded from the Jazz), Kevon Looney, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Collin Sexton, Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams.

Departures: Deandre Ayton (traded to the Wizards), Rui Hachimura (free agent to the Clippers), Jaxson Hayes (free agent to the Jazz), LeBron James (free agent to the Sixers), Luke Kennard (free agent to the Suns), and Marcus Smart (free agent to the Rockets).

Roster: Cameron Carr, Luka Doncic, Quentin Grimes, Jaden Hardy, Bronny James, Arthur Kaluma, Walker Kessler, Dalton Knecht, Jake LaRavia, Kevon Looney, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Chris Manon, AK Okereke, Austin Reaves, Collin Sexton, Adou Thiero, Matisse Thybulle, Jarred Vanderbilt, and Ziaire Williams.

Possible starting five: L. Doncic, A. Reaves, Q. Grimes, J. LaRavia and W. Kessler.

An era of many shadows came to an end with the long-awaited trade of Ja Morant . The player who was supposed to lead the franchise’s past, present, and future projects ended up, for off-court reasons, sidelined and reduced to nothing. And the Grizzlies are already moving toward placing themselves in the hands of another young talent, rookie Cameron Boozer , the No. 3 pick in the Draft. In addition, Memphis also decided to trade Santi Aldama , so aside from Edey , the starting center, and the first rotations, there will be very little left that resembles the team’s recent past. Another year with 25 wins would be hard to endure.

Additions: Jerami Grant (traded from the Trail Blazers), Kris Murray (traded from the Trail Blazers), Micah Peavy (traded from the Pelicans), Quinten Post and Isaiah Stewart (traded from the Pistons).

Departures: Santi Aldama (traded to the Mavericks), Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Taj Gibson (traded to the Pelicans) and Ja Morant (traded to the Trail Blazers).

Roster: Cameron Boozer, Walter Clayton Jr., Carson Cooper, Cedric Coward, Zach Edey, Jerami Grant, Taylor Hendricks, GG Jackson, Ty Jerome, Karim Lopez, Jahmai Mashack, Kris Murray, Micah Peavy, Scotty Pippen Jr., Quinten Post, Olivier-Maxence Prosper, Javon Small, Cam Spencer, Isaiah Stewart and Jaylen Wells.

Possible starting five: T. Jerome, C. Coward, J. Wells, C. Boozer and Z. Edey.

Minnesota moves in the West one step below Thunder and Spurs and with the question of whether it will be able to lead the group of teams that want to disrupt that order. It remains a roster with at least 50 wins in its hands, and the radical change with the addition of LaMelo Ball could help it improve. Ball will form an explosive backcourt duo with Anthony Edwards and could even make him even better. The question is how the departure of important players from last year such as Julius Randle, Nazr Reid and Mike Conley will impact the team. The arrival of Jonathan Kuminga should partly make up for those absences.

Renewals: Jaylen Clark, Ayo Dosunmu (four years) and Bones Hyland.

Additions: LaMelo Ball (traded from the Hornets), Jonathan Kuminga, Trey Lyles and Cody Williams (traded from the Jazz).

Departures: Kyle Anderson (free agent to the Raptors), Mike Conley (free agent to the Celtics), John Konchar (waived), Julius Randle (traded to the Nets) and Naz Reid (traded to the Hornets).

Roster: LaMelo Ball, Joan Beringer, Jaylen Clark, Donte DiVincenzo, Ayo Dosunmu, Anthony Edwards, Isaiah Evans, Rudy Gobert, Bones Hyland, Jonathan Kuminga, Trey Lyles, Jaden McDaniels, Zyon Pullin, Terrence Shannon Jr., Cody Williams and Rocco Zikarsky.

Possible starting five: L. Ball, A. Edwards, J. Kuminga, J. McDaniels and R. Gobert.

Little can be expected from a team coming off winning 26 games the previous year and whose biggest change is at head coach. The arrival of Jamahl Mosley , the third coach since Joe Dumars took charge of the franchise in 2025, speaks to the instability of their projects. This year it will once again be as unreliable as its leader, Zion Williamson , who always raises doubts with his physical condition and his limited capacity for commitment. Even so, the signing of Mathurin adds physical power and points, but the present will be defined by recovering the best version of Dejounte Murray and the future by the growth of its young talents, especially Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen . With Mosley on board, the idea is to finally find an identity.

Renewals: Saddiq Bey (for years) and DeAndre Jordan (one year).

Additions: AJ Johnson (traded from the Grizzlies), Bennedict Mathurin and Trendon Watford.

Departures: Jordan Hawkins (traded to the Grizzlies), Kevon Looney (free agent to the Lakers) and Micah Peavy (traded to the Grizzlies).

Roster: Saddiq Bey, Malik Dia, Jeremiah Fears, AJ Johnson, Herbert Jones, DeAndre Jordan, Bennedict Mathurin, Karlo Matkovic, Bryce McGowens, Yves Missi, Trey Murphy III, Dejounte Murray, Jaron Pierre Jr., Jordan Poole, Derik Queen, Julian Reese, Trendon Watford and Zion Williamson.

" Possible starting five: D. Murray, T. Murphy III, H. Jones, Z. Williamson and Y. Missi.

The champions from two seasons ago are walking a fine line between maintaining a roster capable of contending for the title and a healthy salary cap . Any wrong move will change the franchise’s outlook one way or the other. That is why the Thunder traded players such as Dort, Joe and Wiggins, eroding some of their potential in the second unit, while trusting in the development of players like Mitchell, Wallace and McCain . The arrival of Aday Mara is also exciting because of his great preseason, although the Spaniard will have to grow (in his game, of course). They keep their core starters, but the question is whether they have weakened their rotations enough that they cannot compete with the Spurs . In principle, they rank with San Antonio among the favorites.

Renewals: Isaiah Hartenstein (three years) and Kenrich Williams (one year).

Additions: Aday Mara and Bennett Stirtz

Departures: Branden Carlson (free agent to the Trail Blazers), Luguentz Dort (traded to the Hawks), Isaiah Joe (traded to the Pistons) and Aaron Wiggins (traded to the Hawks).

Roster: Brooks Barnhizer, Alex Caruso, Josh Dix, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Isaiah Hartenstein, Chet Holmgren, Aday Mara, Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell, Otega Oweh, Thomas Sorber, Bennett Stirtz, Nikola Topic, Cason Wallace, Jalen Williams, Jaylin Williams and Kenrich Williams.

Possible starting five: S. Gilgeous-Alexander, C. Wallace, J. Williams, C. Holmgren and I. Hartenstein.

After a surprising season with 45 wins , despite a quick Playoff exit, the Suns have had a busy summer focused mainly on renewals in an attempt to keep their roster intact. The arrivals should only bring positive things, such as that of Bridges , another points creator to pair with Booker , and that of Kennard , a fine shooter to stretch defenses. The bad news is in the infirmary with the injury to the newly re-signed Mark Williams , which will cause him to miss the first months of competition.

Renewals: Dillon Brooks (three years), Collin Gillespie (four years), Jordan Goodwin (three years), Haywood Highsmith (one year) and Mark Williams (three years).

Additions: Miles Bridges (traded from the Hormets), Luke Kennard and Koa Peat.

Departures: Grayson Allen (traded to the Hornets) and Royce O’Neale (traded to the Hornets).

The Trail Blazers , not very active in the market and not at all in the Draft , are going to face two enormous gambles this season. The first is to see how much Damian Lillard has recovered, after sitting out his first year back in Portland . The second is to keep Ja Morant under control on and off the court, after he slipped out the back door of the Grizzlies where he was set to define an era. That, along with getting to know their third coach in 12 months, Micah Nori , will shape the season of a team that returned to the Playoffs after four years away but does not have its place guaranteed in the season that is now beginning.

Renewals: Robert Williams III (three years).

Additions: Branden Carlson. Ja Morant (traded from the Grizzlies), Micah Potter and Jeremy Sochan.

Departures: Jerami Grant (traded to the Grizzlies), Kris Murray (traded to the Grizzlies) and Matisse Thybulle (free agent to the Lakers).

Possible starting five: D. Lillard, J. Morant, T. Camara, D. Avdija and D. Clingan.

The Kings , with 22 wins last season, will face another season with many defeats and with their hopes pinned on the younger players and their development. Meanwhile, they will pray that players like LaVine, Sabonis or Murray do not miss many games through injury, as happened last season, and that Simmons , one of their bets on the market, fits into the team as soon as possible.

Renewals: Precious Achiuwa (two years) and Daeqwon Plowden (two years).

Departures: Devin Carter (traded to the Hawks) and DeMar DeRozan (free agent to the Nuggets).

When a team reaches the Conference Finals and plays in the Finals and not only does it not weaken its roster but actually strengthens it, it automatically becomes the clear favorite to make it back to the championship stage. The Spurs have taken several steps toward their immediate future with the signing of Tobias Harris , who can step straight into the starting lineup, and many more toward their medium- and long-term future with the five-year extension of Victor Wembanyama, a hugely significant strategic move. Last year, the Finals may have come a little too soon for them. This year they will be better prepared and more dangerous.

Additions: Tobias Harris (two years).

For the immediate future, the team will be in a position to improve on last year’s 22 wins and perhaps get involved in some kind of battle for the Play-In .

paragraphs: Unless teams like the Nuggets , the Wolves , the Rockets , or, to a lesser extent, the Lakers , raise some doubts, everything seems to indicate that the Western Conference is heading toward a new final between the Spurs and the Thunder.

And in that battle, the Texans start with an advantage, having strengthened their extraordinary roster—the one that played in the NBA Finals —with Tobias Harris , while Oklahoma continue searching for the balance between saving money and competitiveness. For San Antonio , the Finals arrived ahead of schedule, but 2027 could already be their moment. Their leader, Victor Wembanyama , could even become the fifth non-American player to win the MVP consecutively.

Although there were some changes to the roster, with the departure of Klay Thompson and the arrival of Santi Aldama, the biggest developments for the Mavs came in the front office. The acquisition of Masai Ujiri gives the team the architect of the Toronto Raptors ' 2019 title. And his first decision was to part ways with Jason Kidd and bring in a breath of fresh air in Dusty May, former coach of the NCAA champion Michigan Wolverines . This year's Mavs will have a strong Spanish presence with Santi Aldama , a veteran expected to make an immediate impact, as is Marcus Sasser , and with Sergio de Larrea , who could see plenty of time on the court. The season will depend on how well Kyrie Irving has recovered.
Renewals: Moussa Cissé (two years) and Naji Marshall (three years).
Additions: Santi Aldama (traded from the Grizzlies), Tarik Biberović (two years), Zaccharie Risacher and Marcus Sasser (traded from the Pistons).

Departures: Marvin Bagley III (free agent to the Nuggets), AJ Johnson (traded to the Grizzlies), Khris Middleton (traded to the Wizards), Ryan Nembhard, Klay Thompson (free agent to the Heat) and Brandon Williams (free agent to the Warriors).

Far from strengthening their roster, the Nuggets ' efforts in the preseason focused on trying to retain Peyton Watson , something they were unable to do. The loss of the promising 24-year-old forward has left a significant gap in an expensive roster and raised concern in the front office about trying to avoid being above the second apron of the salary cap again.

Athletically, another scorer arrives, DeMar DeRozan , who should ease those duties for Jokic and Murray . The pair will continue to be the barometer of a team that aspires to win the championship again (before the Jokic era runs out), despite the initial disadvantage against Thunder and Spurs in the West.
Renewals: Tyus Jones (one year) and Spencer Jones (two years).
Additions: Marvin Bagley III (one year), DeMar DeRozan (one year) and Alpha Diallo (one year).
Departures: Tim Hardaway Jr. (free agent to the Heat) and Peyton Watson (traded to the Cavs).

The Warriors officially decided to delay the start of any rebuilding process with the contract extension for Stephen Curry . The veteran point guard will continue to be the player the project relies on, helped by other veterans such as Jimmy Butler, Al Horford, Draymond Green, and Kristaps Porzingis . That said, they managed to protect their future Draft picks and will soon have cap space. But as far as the present is concerned, the team will try to improve on last year's 37 wins in an attempt to avoid having to go through the Play-In. Although climbing higher than eighth place may be more than a complicated goal.

Especially harsh was the one two years ago, when despite having the second-best record in the West, they were eliminated by the seventh seed, Golden State . Out of those two disappointments, a team has grown that could try to join the battle between the Spurs and the Thunder for the conference throne. They re-signed Tari Eason for a little over 80 million and added two veterans to their roster in Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic . They start out on the second tier of favorites in the West .

In exchange for Kawhi they get Brandon Ingram , a player as talented as he is disappointing and unreliable, and they acquired Rai Hachimura who may find with the neighboring L.A. the leading role he was asking for with the Lakers . This year it will once again be as unreliable as its leader, Zion Williamson , who always raises doubts with his physical condition and his limited capacity for commitment. Even so, the signing of Mathurin adds physical power and points, but the present will be defined by recovering the best version of Dejounte Murray and the future by the growth of its young talents, especially Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen . With Mosley on board, the idea is to finally find an identity.

articles.standfirst: Rosters, moves, starting fives and preview of the 15 teams in the Eastern Conference
articles.summary: Rosters, moves, starting fives and preview of the 15 teams in the Eastern Conference
articles.body:
The Eastern Conference gets underway with a new title contender. The Sixers' moves in signing Jaylen Brown and LeBron James have turned the Sixers into the team with the best starting five in the entire NBA. It only remains to be seen whether their bench will allow them to stop being contenders and become champions. They have not won a title since 1983.

Alongside them, the Knicks want to repeat and know that at the end of the season they will lose some of their key players. The current roster, with few changes, has a good chance to reach glory, but the franchise will play for the first time since 1973 without the pressure of having to win the title. Cleveland, Detroit, Miami and Boston will seek a place in the Conference Finals and who knows, perhaps in the NBA Finals, while Indiana and Washington could be two of the most improved teams of the season.

The Atlanta Hawks will experience their first full season following the trade of what had been their great star in the past, Trae Young . They have dived into the market to strengthen their bench, with players like Aaron Wiggins, Luguentz Dort and Dorian Finney-Smith , all of them with proven experience in the League, and above all they have managed to retain CJ McCollum , who will be their reference point and their guide this season.

Expectations are high for the Hawks because they feel they are heading into the regular season with a better roster than in previous years despite the January trade of Young and having let go of their 2024 No. 1 pick, Zaccharie Risacher . Even so, it will not be easy at all to repeat last year's sixth-place finish (46-36) only to fall in the first round to the Knicks (4-2).

Renewals: Jock Landale (one year) and CJ McCollum (one year).

Additions: Luguentz Dort (traded from the Thunder), Dorian Finney-Smith (traded from the Hornets), and Aaron Wiggins (traded from the Thunder).

Departures: Buddy Hield (traded to the Hornets), Jonathan Kuminga (free agent) and Zaccharie Risacher (traded to the Mavericks).

Roster: Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, RayJ Dennis, Luguentz Dort, Zuby Ejiofor, Dorian Finney-Smith, Kingston Flemings, Keshon Gilbert, Mouhamed Gueye, Jalen Johnson, Corey Kispert, Jock Landale, CJ McCollum, Asa Newell, Onyeka Okongwu, Henri Veesaar, Aaron Wiggins and Jalen Wilson.

Possible starting five: C. McCollum, N. Alexander-Walker, D. Daniels, J. Johnson and O. Okongwu.

When the Celtics decided to trade Jaylen Brown, they officially began a rebuilding process. They had already started it a year earlier, with the trades of Jrue Holiday and Kristaps Porzingis , but letting your best player of the last few seasons go is a statement of intent. In exchange for Brown , they get Paul George and several Draft picks. No miracle is expected from George in Boston , especially not with his eternal physical problems, while the Draft picks are considered a treasure for the short- and medium-term future.

The Celtics will continue to press the pace with quick transition play and three-point shooting, to Mazzulla 's liking, along with changes in the interior game with the arrival of Mitchell Robinson . Hugo González will have to step up in an important year for him and for some Celtics who must reinvent their competitive formula. They start out on the second tier of favorites in the East.

But Chicago heads into this year with renewed hopes, turning their No. 4 draft pick, Caleb Wilson , into their new icon for the future, while also surrounding him with the experience of Nick Claxton or Norman Powell . They are also the only team whose highest salary, that of Josh Giddey , does not exceed 25 million. In other words, they still have plenty of salary cap space to use. The Cavs spent too long in the preseason bogged down by the possible homecoming of LeBron James, which ultimately fell through. However, Cleveland hasn't done badly at all because the Nuggets' financial problems handed them Payton Watson on a silver platter after he signed an outstanding season in Colorado.

His impact will be immediate and he will go straight into the starting five, where, among others, James Harden and Donovan Mitchell will be waiting for him, and they will appreciate his defensive skills; they were also in the spotlight during the preseason because of their respective contract extensions. The Cavs also include Khalifa Diop on their roster and, above all, Mario Hezonja back in the NBA; we will see whether it is to stay.

The goal for the Cavs is to return to the Eastern Finals and take one more step toward playing in the NBA Finals.

And as the season unfolds, Miami's front office will make moves in that direction. Mainly because the mammoth move they made cost them some key pieces, such as Herro, Ware and Jaquez , and they did not land the Powell signing they were pursuing. Even so, they did bring in other pieces like Portis, Hardaway or Thompson , who should have an immediate impact. The problem with reaching the top is that the demands are, at the very least (and at most), to do it again the following year. And that, in the NBA, is very complicated. The Knicks already know that no team has repeated since 2018, and that is why their mission is enormous. And during the preseason, the fear at Madison was that the championship roster would fall apart, after owner James Dolan made sure they would not go over the dreaded second apron. The result is the loss of a key piece, Mitchell Robinson , but also the lower-cost renewals of some luxury backups, such as Clarkson , Alvarado , Shamet or Diawara in an attempt to repeat, while keeping the championship core intact. The Knicks start out in "pole position" alongside the Sixers in the East.

With the Magic he will have the talent of the core group that reached the Playoffs via the Play-In ( Paolo Banchero, Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane ), and that had the Eastern Conference leaders, the Pistons, on the ropes (3-1) until Wagner got injured. Incidentally, Mo's departure as a free agent to Brooklyn separates the German brothers for the first time in their careers.

With that trade, Nick Nurse ’s team crossed the line and established itself as the clear favorite in the East. They also added solid reinforcements in Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope , and the departures will barely have any impact, especially that of Paul George , who leaves Philadelphia without much fuss or fanfare. No NBA team has changed its fortunes as much in recent months as the Sixers . That said, anything short of at least reaching the Finals will not be enough.

Trying to rebuild around Trae Young and Anthony Davis , the Wizards should not cross paths with the word tanking again. Their defeats last year (third with more than 60 games lost) paid off: AJ Dybantsa at number 1 in the Draft. That, veterans like Khris Middleton and DeAndre Ayton , and young players who should start to have a bigger role in the rotations such as Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George, Tre Johnson and Will Riley suggest a season with multiple green shoots in the capital. It has been eight seasons since the Wi z ards won more games than they lost, and five since they last set foot in Playoffs territory. Both streaks could come to an end.

paragraphs: The Eastern Conference gets underway with a new title contender. The Sixers' moves in signing Jaylen Brown and LeBron James have turned the Sixers into the team with the best starting five in the entire NBA. It only remains to be seen whether their bench will allow them to stop being contenders and become champions. They have not won a title since 1983.

Alongside them, the Knicks want to repeat and know that at the end of the season they will lose some of their key players. The current roster, with few changes, has a good chance to reach glory, but the franchise will play for the first time since 1973 without the pressure of having to win the title. Cleveland, Detroit, Miami and Boston will seek a place in the Conference Finals and who knows, perhaps in the NBA Finals, while Indiana and Washington could be two of the most improved teams of the season.

The Atlanta Hawks will experience their first full season following the trade of what had been their great star in the past, Trae Young . They have dived into the market to strengthen their bench, with players like Aaron Wiggins, Luguentz Dort and Dorian Finney-Smith , all of them with proven experience in the League, and above all they have managed to retain CJ McCollum , who will be their reference point and their guide this season.

Expectations are high for the Hawks because they feel they are heading into the regular season with a better roster than in previous years despite the January trade of Young and having let go of their 2024 No. 1 pick, Zaccharie Risacher . Even so, it will not be easy at all to repeat last year's sixth-place finish (46-36) only to fall in the first round to the Knicks (4-2).

Additions: Luguentz Dort (traded from the Thunder), Dorian Finney-Smith (traded from the Hornets), and Aaron Wiggins (traded from the Thunder).

Possible starting five: C. Cunningham, D. Robinson, A. Thompson, J. Collins and J. Duren.

Last season, the Pacers struggled near the bottom of the Eastern standings. They finished second to last with 19 wins, 31 fewer than the previous season, the one in which they reached the Finals . And one might think that this year will be more of the same because they have not made major moves in the preseason market; however, their roster has received two major morale boosts with the return of Tyrese Haliburton , injured since the 2025 Finals, and of Ivica Zubak, signed from the Clippers midway through last season and who barely played five games. With the two of them, Indiana , at the very least, will have the tools to fight for a spot in the Play-In, although a deep rebuild looms on the horizon.
Additions: Larry Nance Jr. (one year) and Kelly Oubre Jr. (two years).
Departures: Kam Jones (traded to the Bulls) and Micah Potter (waived).

Roster: Kobe Brown, Johnny Furphy, Tyrese Haliburton, Jay Huff, Quenton Jackson, T.J. McConnell, Larry Nance Jr., Andrew Nembhard, Aaron Nesmith, Kelly Oubre Jr., Ben Sheppard, Pascal Siakam, Jalen Slawson, Braden Smith, Obi Toppin, Jarace Walker and Ivica Zubac.
Possible starting five: T. Haliburton, A. Nembhard, A. Nesmith, P. Siakam and I. Zubac.

Any team that had managed to trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo would automatically become a title contender. The Heat are, although it feels like something is still missing to complete the roster. And as the season unfolds, Miami's front office will make moves in that direction. Mainly because the mammoth move they made cost them some key pieces, such as Herro, Ware and Jaquez , and they did not land the Powell signing they were pursuing. Even so, they did bring in other pieces like Portis, Hardaway or Thompson , who should have an immediate impact. They got distracted by the possibility of LeBron choosing Miami , something that sectors of the Heat viewed as more than unlikely. With Giannis , they will be in the fight in the East.
Renewals: Simone Fontecchio (one year), Pelle Larsson (four years) and Andrew Wiggins (three years).
Additions: Giannis Antetokounmpo (traded from the Bucks), Tim Hardaway Jr., Bobby Portis (traded from the Bucks), Nick Richards (one year) and Klay Thompson (two years).

Departures: Tyler Herro (traded to the Bucks), Kasparas Jakučionis (traded to the Bucks), Jaime Jaquez Jr. (traded to the Bucks), Norman Powell (traded to the Bulls) andKel’el Ware (traded to the Bucks).

Roster: Bam Adebayo, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Ryan Conwell, Tre Donaldson, Simone Fontecchio, Myron Gardner, Vladislav Goldin, Tim Hardaway Jr., Keshad Johnson, Nikola Jovic, Pelle Larsson, Davion Mitchell, Bobby Portis, Nick Richards, Dru Smith, Klay Thompson and Andrew Wiggins.
Possible starting five: D. Mitchell, K. Thompson, A. Wiggins, G. Antetokounmpo and B. Adebayo.

The same as the Heat , but the other way around. Any team that trades away its biggest star stops being a contender. And that is what happens to the Bucks as they see an era come to an end with Giannis Antetokounmpo as their leader for 13 years. The Greek's departure officially begins Milwaukee 's rebuilding process, although they had already been laying the groundwork for a couple of seasons. Taylor Jenkings arrives with a new philosophy, many new players, but low expectations. It will be another year without the postseason.
Renewals: Ousmane Dieng (three years), Bogoljub Marković (multi-year contract), Pete Nance (two years) and Gary Trent Jr. (four years).

Additions: Tyler Herro (traded from the Heat), Kasparas Jakučionis (traded from the Heat), Jaime Jaquez Jr. (traded from the Heat), Caris LeVert (traded from the Pistons), and Kel’el Ware (traded from the Heat).
Departures: Giannis Antetokounmpo (traded to the Heat), Gary Harris (traded to the Pistons), Bobby Portis (traded to the Heat) and Taurean Prince (traded to the Pistons).

The problem with reaching the top is that the demands are, at the very least (and at most), to do it again the following year. And that, in the NBA, is very complicated. The Knicks already know that no team has repeated since 2018, and that is why their mission is enormous. And during the preseason, the fear at Madison was that the championship roster would fall apart, after owner James Dolan made sure they would not go over the dreaded second apron. The result is the loss of a key piece, Mitchell Robinson , but also the lower-cost renewals of some luxury backups, such as Clarkson , Alvarado , Shamet or Diawara in an attempt to repeat, while keeping the championship core intact. The Knicks start out in "pole position" alongside the Sixers in the East.
Renewals: Jose Alvarado (three years), Jordan Clarkson (one year), Mohamed Diawara (multi-year contract), and Landry Shamet (four years).
Additions: Andre Drummond (one year).
Departures: Ariel Hukporti (free agent to the Sixers), Mitchell Robinson (free agent to the Celtics) and Jeremy Sochan (free agent to the Trail Blazers).

The most radical change for the Magic this season is not on the court, but on the bench. After five seasons, they fired Jamahl Mosley (now with the Pelicans ) and entrusted the team to Sean Sweeney, the sixteenth coach in franchise history, who arrives with a Spurs ring after having been part of the Texans' coaching staff. With the Magic he will have the talent of the core group that reached the Playoffs via the Play-In ( Paolo Banchero, Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane ), and that had the Eastern Conference leaders, the Pistons, on the ropes (3-1) until Wagner got injured. Incidentally, Mo's departure as a free agent to Brooklyn separates the German brothers for the first time in their careers.
Renewals: Jevon Carter (one year) and Jonathan Isaac (one year).
Additions: Nikola Vučević (one year).
Departures: Moritz Wagner (free agent to the Nets).

Roster: Paolo Banchero, Desmond Bane, Goga Bitadze, Anthony Black, Jamal Cain, Jevon Carter, Wendell Carter Jr., Colin Castleton, Tristan da Silva, Jonathan Isaac, Alex Morales, Izaiyah Nelson, Noah Penda, Jase Richardson, Jalen Suggs, Nikola Vucevic, and Franz Wagner.

When LeBron James chose the Sixers , there was talk that Philly was the top title contender, but they had taken the step toward that earlier, when they got ahead of everyone to land Jaylen Brown . With that trade, Nick Nurse ’s team crossed the line and established itself as the clear favorite in the East. They also added solid reinforcements in Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope , and the departures will barely have any impact, especially that of Paul George , who leaves Philadelphia without much fuss or fanfare. No NBA team has changed its fortunes as much in recent months as the Sixers . That said, anything short of at least reaching the Finals will not be enough.
Additions: Jaylen Brown (traded from the Celtics), Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Ariel Hukporti, LeBron James (two years), Anfernee Simons (two years), and Dean Wade (four years).

The NBA's investigation into the Clippers ' salary cap cheating delayed and shaped the Raptors ' preseason and the return of the prodigal son. Kawhi Leonard, several years older, will once again be the leader of a team that will see virtually no changes to its starting five, except for Kawhi , of course. The 46 wins from last year can serve as a benchmark to measure the team, but what the Raptors want is to win a Playoff round for the first time since 2020.
Renewals: Alijah Martin (two years) and Jamal Shead (three years).
Additions: Kyle Anderson (one year) and Kawhi Leonard (traded from the Clippers).
Departures: Gradey Dick (traded to the Clippers), Brandon Ingram (traded to the Clippers), and Sandro Mamukelashvili (free agent to the Lakers).

Trying to rebuild around Trae Young and Anthony Davis , the Wizards should not cross paths with the word tanking again. Their defeats last year (third with more than 60 games lost) paid off: AJ Dybantsa at number 1 in the Draft. It has been eight seasons since the Wi z ards won more games than they lost, and five since they last set foot in Playoffs territory. Both streaks could come to an end.

articles.title: Why a glaring weakness will cost LA Lakers the 2027 ring
articles.standfirst: The Lakers have rebuilt their roster around Doncic, yet JJ Redick still faces difficult questions
articles.summary: The Lakers have rebuilt their roster around Doncic, yet JJ Redick still faces difficult questions
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have invested heavily in building a championship contender around Luka Doncic , but their biggest challenge may have little to do with scoring points.

After reshaping the roster following LeBron James ' departure, Los Angeles enters the 2026-27 NBA season with an explosive offensive partnership between Doncic and Austin Reaves, supported by several significant offseason additions.

The two guards combined for 56.8 points per game last season, with the Lakers recording a 30-11 record when both were available.

Those numbers provide considerable encouragement, but the team's defensive limitations could become increasingly difficult to conceal against opponents capable of exploiting mismatches.

The arrival of Walker Kessler from the Utah Jazz was designed to address one of Los Angeles' most pressing weaknesses.

The 7-foot-2 center signed a four-year, $130 million contract after the Lakers committed substantial draft capital to acquire him.

Kessler provides an imposing presence around the basket, but his effectiveness will depend heavily on the defenders operating in front of him.

Opponents can force switches involving Doncic and Reaves , attack gaps created by screens and repeatedly challenge the Lakers ' ability to contain penetration.

That places additional pressure on Kessler , who must decide whether to contest shots, protect against passes to opposing centers or compensate for teammates beaten on the perimeter.

The departures of experienced defenders, including Marcus Smart , have only increased the importance of Los Angeles finding consistent solutions.

Difficult challenge with revamped Lakers roster

Head coach JJ Redick has several candidates capable of helping address those concerns, including Quentin Grimes, Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams .

Los Angeles experimented with aggressive full-court defensive pressure during the preseason, demonstrating its potential during a 127-103 victory over the Sacramento Kings .

However, maintaining that approach against elite playoff opponents will require discipline, particularly when initial pressure fails and defenders must recover into half-court positions.

Redick believes his new players understand the expectations attached to representing the Lakers.

"All these guys that haven't gone through it, there's nothing like it," he said. "And I think they all want to embrace it. They all have a chip on their shoulder about it. They want to make Lakers fans proud, and I know they will."

The challenge is turning that enthusiasm into defensive consistency across an entire season.

Luka Doncic embraces championship expectations

Despite the uncertainty, Doncic has welcomed the franchise's aggressive approach to roster construction.

The Slovenian superstar was involved in discussions surrounding Kessler 's acquisition and expressed enthusiasm about playing alongside the former Utah center.

"There was a lot of communication with Rob and JJ about him," Doncic said. "So I'm very excited to just share the floor with him."

Doncic also hosted his new teammates for an offseason gathering in Slovenia, helping establish relationships before the campaign begins.

Grimes believes that experience has already strengthened the group's chemistry.

"Everybody came in ego-less," he said. "And I feel like everybody really bought into the role of what they need to do on this team."

Los Angeles now faces the challenge of translating that chemistry into results against Western Conference contenders such as the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs .

The Lakers possess enough offensive talent to challenge those opponents, but postseason success will ultimately depend on whether their defensive improvements prove sustainable.

Without reliable perimeter resistance, even Kessler 's considerable shot-blocking ability may not be enough to deliver another championship.

articles.title: LeBron James steals the spotlight at Jaylen Brown’s 30th birthday party with sharp tuxedo look
articles.summary: LeBron James showed up in style at teammate Jaylen Brown’s 30th birthday party, arriving in a tuxedo for what appeared to be a black-tie celebration. The Lakers star quickly became one of the most photographed guests, proving that even among a room full of celebrities, the King remains a star in his own right. James made a point of greeting the birthday boy as soon as he arrived, with cameras capturing the moment he wished Brown a happy birthday and made it clear he was ready to celebrate. Brown could not stop smiling as he welcomed James to the party, highlighting the bond between two of the NBA’s biggest names. Their growing connection continues to draw attention from fans, who are keeping a close eye on this new dynamic duo.

articles.title: A past mistake by LeBron James resurfaces as he talks about Dalton Knecht
articles.standfirst: He was the player competing with Bronny James for a spot on the Lakers roster… and ended up being the one sacrificed.
articles.summary: He was the player competing with Bronny James for a spot on the Lakers roster… and ended up being the one sacrificed.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers surprised many on Monday by waiving Dalton Knecht as part of the moves needed to comply with the NBA ’s roster limit. The decision frustrated a number of fans, especially given that only a few months earlier the young wing was viewed as one of the higher-upside pieces in the franchise’s future.

The Lakers selected Knecht with the 17th overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft , betting on an offensive specialist with strong three-point shooting ability. His development never matched those expectations, and he is now off the Los Angeles roster.

The situation has once again put LeBron James in the spotlight. Although James is no longer with the team, an old public endorsement of the then-rookie resurfaced on social media and sparked debate among fans:

“They didn’t find DK… the other 16 teams f****d it up. Did anybody watch him?”

With those words, LeBron criticized the teams that selected ahead of the Lakers and made clear that he saw Knecht as a player with the potential to become an important piece for the franchise.

There was even a perception that Los Angeles had drafted Knecht specifically to give LeBron a new shooter who could capitalize on his passes and create spacing on offense.

Knecht showed some promising moments early in his Lakers tenure, but his standing changed when he was included in a proposed trade with the Charlotte Hornets for Mark Williams . Concerns about the big man’s physical condition caused Los Angeles to cancel the deal and reclaim Knecht. His confidence and role within the team never fully recovered afterward.

LeBron James’ bet on Dalton Knecht did not pan out

LeBron’s support for Knecht stood out because it went beyond a routine endorsement of a rookie. The four-time NBA champion genuinely believed in his talent and viewed him as part of the Lakers’ young core alongside Austin Reaves.

James had previously demonstrated a strong eye for talent by speaking positively about Reaves before the guard developed into one of the team’s key figures.

However, LeBron’s track record as a talent evaluator also includes notable misses. One of the most remembered is Shabazz Napier , a college prospect James once highlighted as a potential NBA star. The Miami Heat selected Napier in the 2014 Draft partly with an eye toward keeping LeBron satisfied. James left the franchise shortly afterward to return to the Cleveland Cavaliers , and Napier never became the player many expected.

Now, Dalton Knecht may become another example of a player in whom James identified special qualities that ultimately failed to translate into consistent NBA impact.

articles.title: The San Antonio Spurs tipped to win the NBA title: “This is their year”
articles.standfirst: Pepe Brasín broke down the start of the 2026-27 NBA season on ‘Las Brasas de Brasín,’ tipping Victor Wembanyama as a leading MVP contender and assessing the Spanish players’ prospects and the league’s tanking problem.
articles.summary: Pepe Brasín broke down the start of the 2026-27 NBA season on ‘Las Brasas de Brasín,’ tipping Victor Wembanyama as a leading MVP contender and assessing the Spanish players’ prospects and the league’s tanking problem.
articles.body:
The NBA is back, and Pepe Brasín knows exactly where his attention is focused. The La Tribu contributor used his regular Brasas de Brasín segment to break down the start of the 2026-27 season and name the team he believes is best positioned to win the championship: the San Antonio Spurs. That prediction centers on Victor Wembanyama, who Brasín believes is ready to establish himself as the biggest star in world basketball.

“I think the feeling around the NBA is that this is the San Antonio Spurs’ year,” Brasín said. He linked their title hopes directly to the French star’s development: “This is the year Victor Wembanyama truly reaches superstardom and becomes the best player in the world.”

Wembanyama aiming for it all

Brasín believes the French center is ready to dominate the league in several areas. His prediction goes beyond Wembanyama’s individual performance and also extends to San Antonio’s championship aspirations. “MVP candidate, Defensive Player of the Year candidate, and the top favorites to win the championship,” he said when describing what he expects from the Spurs and their star.

However, the journalist acknowledged that the season itself will ultimately determine whether those expectations are justified. “Fortunately, we have an entire season to find all of that out,” he added. He also highlighted other storylines heading into the new campaign, including LeBron James’ move to a new team, the Philadelphia 76ers and the New York Knicks’ title defense.

For Brasín, the NBA has one major strength that explains much of its appeal: “The NBA’s ability to create stories and generate interest is almost endless.”

The NBA’s major problem remains unresolved

It wasn’t all praise. Brasín devoted a significant part of his analysis to tanking, the strategy used by some teams to prioritize their position in the NBA Draft once their chances of competing for meaningful goals begin to fade. “It’s a very serious problem for the NBA,” he said.

His main criticism is aimed at franchises that stop prioritizing wins as the season progresses: “Around January or February, a third of the league decides it doesn’t want to keep playing, that it doesn’t want to keep competing.”

He is also unconvinced by the changes to the draft system designed to combat the practice. “They changed the draft format, quite clumsily in my opinion. I don’t like the changes they’ve made at all,” he said.

Brasín believes spreading the chances of landing the No. 1 pick among more teams does not remove the incentive to lose games. “Competing without actually needing to win games is an aberration and a disaster for the NBA,” he said. And he does not expect the problem to disappear quickly: “Things don’t change overnight. It takes a long time, several years.”

Spain’s new generation looks to make its mark

The start of the season also brings reasons for optimism for Spanish basketball. Brasín highlighted young players such as Aday Mara, Sergio de Larrea and Baba Miller, along with the development of others who already have NBA experience. “Aday Mara is a very intriguing player, very intriguing,” he said of the center, who faces competition from Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein with the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Brasín believes potential financial challenges with the Thunder roster could eventually create opportunities for Mara. “I don’t know if it will happen this year, and I don’t know if he’ll get many minutes, but I think the Thunder want Aday Mara to become an important part of their immediate future,” he explained.

He also discussed Hugo González, who could take on a bigger role in Boston, and Santi Aldama, whom he believes could find a place in Dallas. Spanish basketball may still be some way from the era of Pau and Marc Gasol, but Brasín sees encouraging signs: “We’re not where we were two or three years ago when it comes to Spanish basketball.”

With San Antonio among the favorites, a new generation of talent emerging and questions surrounding the league’s competitiveness, Brasín is thrilled to see the NBA return. “I love it. I’m crazy about it,” he said.

His main criticism is aimed at franchises that stop prioritizing wins as the season progresses: “Around January or February, a third of the league decides it doesn’t want to keep playing, that it doesn’t want to keep competing.”

He is also unconvinced by the changes to the draft system designed to combat the practice. “They changed the draft format, quite clumsily in my opinion. I don’t like the changes they’ve made at all,” he said.

Brasín believes spreading the chances of landing the No. 1 pick among more teams does not remove the incentive to lose games. “Competing without actually needing to win games is an aberration and a disaster for the NBA,” he said. And he does not expect the problem to disappear quickly: “Things don’t change overnight. It takes a long time, several years.”
Spain’s new generation looks to make its mark

The start of the season also brings reasons for optimism for Spanish basketball. Brasín highlighted young players such as Aday Mara, Sergio de Larrea and Baba Miller, along with the development of others who already have NBA experience. “Aday Mara is a very intriguing player, very intriguing,” he said of the center, who faces competition from Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein with the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Brasín believes potential financial challenges with the Thunder roster could eventually create opportunities for Mara. “I don’t know if it will happen this year, and I don’t know if he’ll get many minutes, but I think the Thunder want Aday Mara to become an important part of their immediate future,” he explained.

He also discussed Hugo González, who could take on a bigger role in Boston, and Santi Aldama, whom he believes could find a place in Dallas. Spanish basketball may still be some way from the era of Pau and Marc Gasol, but Brasín sees encouraging signs: “We’re not where we were two or three years ago when it comes to Spanish basketball.”

With San Antonio among the favorites, a new generation of talent emerging and questions surrounding the league’s competitiveness, Brasín is thrilled to see the NBA return. “I love it. I’m crazy about it,” he said.

articles.title: The stars who rule the NBA: Doncic, Jokic, Wembanyama, Brunson, Shai, Antetokounmpo, LeBron, Curry...
articles.standfirst: The league, which specializes in nurturing and promoting its business, always puts them in the spotlight
articles.summary: The league, which specializes in nurturing and promoting its business, always puts them in the spotlight
articles.body:
The NBA has always known that there are players who transcend the court. Stars capable of turning every game into an event and who, each season, add another chapter to their legend. The league, which specializes in nurturing and growing its business, always puts them in the spotlight because they are so much more than their statistics: they are faces, icons, and global role models. These players, blessed with extraordinary talent and a special charisma, carry on their shoulders both the privilege and the responsibility of representing the league’s image. In a way, they are the on-court embodiment of that iconic logo that symbolizes the most powerful basketball league on the planet.

Some have been dominating and building on their legacy for years, such as Nikola Jokic, Kevin Durant, LeBron James, Stephen Curry, and Joel Embiid . Others have burst onto the scene with the impact of players destined to define an era, such as Victor Wembanyama, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, and Anthony Edwards . Then there are those who have elevated their leadership to become the heart of their franchises, such as Jalen Brunson, Jayson Tatum, and Cade Cunningham .

And players whose influence on and off the court completely shapes the present and future of their teams—such as Luka Doncic, Donovan Mitchell, and Giannis Antetokounmpo . A select group of superstars who do much more than just play games: they drive franchises, draw crowds, build legacies, and, to a large extent, shape the course of the NBA.

Luka Doncic: the present and future of the Lakers

Luka Doncic is no longer just the Lakers’ big star. Following LeBron James ’ departure, he is the cornerstone upon which the Los Angeles team is building its present and much of its future. At 27, he is entering the prime of his career—a player who has already earned six All-NBA selections and is coming off his second scoring title in three seasons, averaging 33.48 points per game. His influence has even reached the front office: the franchise granted his request for a top-tier center— Walker Kessler —and made an effort to keep his right-hand man, Austin Reaves , by his side.

But Luka needs to turn his undeniable individual dominance into collective power. With the Lakers, he hasn’t yet replicated the impact he had in Dallas, and his recent playoff record with the team leaves something to be desired. Even so, his ability to rack up points, rebounds, and assists at a pace reserved for legends—he is one of only three players in NBA history, along with Oscar Robertson and LeBron James, to reach 15,000 points, 4,000 rebounds, and 4,000 assists in his first eight seasons—means that any Lakers project inevitably starts with him.

Jalen Brunson: the man who brought the Championship back to New York

Jalen Brunson has gone from being a star to becoming the man who changed New York’s recent history. The 30-year-old point guard led the Knicks to their first championship in more than half a century, also winning the Conference Finals and NBA Finals MVP awards. Three consecutive All-NBA selections and his ability to close out games have made him the true captain of Madison Square Garden .

His impact on the big stage was underscored by a staggering statistic: he averaged 11.2 points in the final quarters of the 2026 Finals, the highest figure in history for a point guard. Brunson doesn’t need to dominate with his size (he’s 1.88 m tall); he does so through control, character, and the ability to make big plays. Now comes the challenge of keeping a champion team—one that has become everyone’s target—on top. The NBA has found in New York’s “little giant” one of its new powerhouses.

Victor Wembanyama knocks on the door to the throne

Victor Wembanyama is fast-forwarding the NBA’s timeline. At just 22 years old and 2.24 m tall, the Frenchman has already been named to the All-NBA Team, won Defensive Player of the Year, and become the first player to unanimously win the Defensive Player of the Year award. His combination of height, mobility, shooting, and ability to impact games on both ends of the court has turned San Antonio into one of the league’s top contenders. The question is no longer whether he will be a superstar, but just how far he can go.

His first experience in the Finals showed just how much room for growth he still has. The Spurs dominated entire stretches of the series, but they were unable to protect their leads when the games entered high-pressure situations. Wemby will need to build up his stamina and gain experience so that his extraordinary defensive impact—he leads the NBA in blocks and in DWS (the number of wins a player contributes to his team through his defensive performance)—can also translate into absolute dominance in June. The player poised to change the landscape of basketball is already knocking on the door of the throne.

Nikola Jokic, the lord and master of the game

Nikola Jokic has turned the extraordinary into routine. For the third consecutive year, the center topped ESPN’s rankings after averaging a triple-double for the second straight season—a feat previously achieved only by Russell Westbrook . He has finished first or second in the MVP voting for six consecutive seasons and has entered a realm where each season seems to demand a new way of measuring his dominance.

The Serbian doesn't need speed or flashiness to control a game: he does it with court vision, precision, and a unique ability to turn every possession into an advantage. Last season, he added yet another mind-boggling feat to his collection of records: he became the first player in history to simultaneously lead the NBA in rebounds and assists per game. His outside shooting suffered after a knee injury, but Denver’s real challenge remains the same: building a team around a player who has turned team play into an extension of his own talent.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander: A third MVP and a second championship ring?

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has stopped trying to emulate the previous generation and has become one of its leading figures. He is the NBA MVP for the second consecutive year, was a champion in 2024–25, and enters the new season with the chance to do something that hasn’t happened since Larry Bird : win three consecutive MVP awards. His style of play combines efficiency, control of the pace, and offensive production that allows him to dominate without needing an excessive number of shots.

The Oklahoma City point guard also embodies the changing of the guard in the NBA. This season, he could become only the third player in history—alongside Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan —to average at least 30 points on 50% shooting for five consecutive seasons. And although the Thunder were unable to make it back to the Finals, their ceiling still depends largely on what happens when Shai has a healthy Jalen Williams by his side: together, Oklahoma City outscored their opponents by 15.3 points per 100 possessions.

Jayson Tatum: the Celtics need him at his best

Jayson Tatum is back in the spotlight after a season marred by an Achilles tendon injury. His return was extraordinarily productive despite having played only 16 regular-season games and six playoff games, and he now has additional months to fully regain the form that earned him a spot on the NBA’s All-NBA First Team for four consecutive years. In Boston, moreover, Jaylen Brown’s departure places even more pressure on the number one spot.

Tatum faces a huge challenge because the Celtics need to get their star player back to full strength. Even before his injury, he had already proven himself to be much more than just a scorer: he is one of only three players—along with Jokic and Giannis—who, over the past two seasons, have consistently averaged at least 25 points, eight rebounds, and five assists per game. If he returns to that level, Boston will once again have one of the key players capable of shifting the balance of power in the Eastern Conference.

Anthony Edwards gets the Wolves roaring

Anthony Edwards embodies the rise of a generation that no longer asks permission to take center stage. At just 25 years old, the Minnesota shooting guard averaged 28.8 points, shot 40% from three-point range on a high volume of attempts, and established himself as one of the league’s top outside threats. During Tatum’s absence, he even earned recognition as the NBA’s best two-way small forward (offense and defense).

His ceiling is yet to be reached. Edwards has already scored 10,854 points before turning 25, trailing only LeBron James and Kevin Durant in NBA history. He still needs to grow as a playmaker for his teammates—an area where he still trails the top superstars in the running for MVP. But his combination of power, audacity, shooting, and ability to rise to the occasion on the big stage has made Minnesota a team whose present and future bear his mark.

Donovan Mitchell, ready to take the throne

Don ovan Mitchell is no longer just the explosive scorer who arrived in Cleveland from Utah. At 30, he has just led the Cavaliers to the Conference Finals for the first time and has been selected to the All-Star Game seven consecutive times. His ability to create off the dribble and use his shooting range to stun defenses makes him the offensive engine of a team that also features James Harden, Evan Mobley, and Jarrett Allen .

Mitchell is one of eight players who have averaged at least 20 points in each of the last nine seasons. Cleveland has talent to spare, but when the moment of truth arrives, much of its success will depend on its shooting guard’s ability to recapture the dominant form he displayed in previous playoffs, when he averaged 30 points per game. Now he’s ready to take the leap that separates a great star from a champion.

Giannis Antetokounmpo: the hurricane arrives in Miami

Giannis Antetokounmpo has changed teams, but not his level of play. The Greek star arrives in Miami after a final season in Milwaukee limited to 36 games, facing the challenge of proving that he remains at the peak of his competitive abilities. If he stays healthy, he will continue to belong to the extraordinarily small group of players capable of combining 30 points, 10 rebounds, and absolute dominance on offense.

His arrival makes the Heat one of the biggest stories of the season. Miami has staked a huge number of assets on the player it considers its new cornerstone, and Giannis brings something few players can offer: the ability to break down a defense by attacking the basket, dominate the boards, and dictate the game through his defense. Furthermore, his presence fits right into a competitive culture built around Pat Riley and Erik Spoelstra . The Heat once again have a superstar capable of single-handedly reshaping the Eastern Conference landscape.

Kevin Durant: the legend who refuses to step off the stage

Kevin Durant is now in a league of his own: that of the legends who remain in the spotlight long after most of their contemporaries have long since faded from the limelight. In his first season in Houston , he averaged 26 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 4.8 assists, shooting 52% from the field and 41.3% from three-point range—numbers that earned him his twelfth All-NBA selection, this time to the Second Team. At 37, he remains one of the most efficient scorers in history.

Durant, moreover, didn’t come to Houston just to be a figurehead. The Rockets made one of the NBA’s biggest moves by signing him and have built a young core around him, led by Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson . Over a 20-season career, KD has amassed two championship rings, two Finals MVP awards, one MVP award, four scoring titles, and 12 All-NBA selections; he has also surpassed 30,000 points. Houston lost in the first round last season and is once again looking to take a competitive leap forward: Durant is the experience, the talent, and the offensive weapon that should help open that door.

Cade Cunningham, the driving force behind the Pistons' dreams

Cade Cunningham is no longer just a prospect—he’s one of the big stars setting the pace in the NBA. At 24, the Detroit Pistons point guard is coming off a season that made a massive impact, earning his first All-NBA First Team selection and leading his franchise to 60 wins—a feat it hadn’t achieved in two decades. His ability to control the pace, exploit matchups, and create plays has firmly established him among the elite, after overcoming injuries and the grueling slump of a team that won only 14 games in 2023–24.

Cunningham’s next step is to address his remaining weakness: turnovers. In the last playoffs, he averaged 5.6 per game—the highest total in history for a player in a series of at least ten games. But much of that burden also stems from the responsibility he shoulders on a Pistons team that needs another great playmaker alongside him. Detroit has an immediate window of opportunity ahead of it, and the franchise’s future hinges on building around Cunningham, who is already operating in the realm of the NBA’s biggest stars.

LeBron James, the King, is reluctant to give up his throne

At 41, LeBron James remains one of the great figures who set the tone for the NBA. His longevity is unprecedented: last season, he played in 60 games and averaged 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds, and 7.2 assists, along with a 51.5% field goal percentage. He continues to be capable of creating plays, scoring, and influencing the outcome of games despite the passage of time. His impact goes beyond the statistics, and he remains one of the league’s greatest icons.

He now faces a new challenge in Philadelphia , where he joins the Sixers, who aim to turn the talent of Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, and LeBron himself into a team capable of contending for the championship. His experience, his ability to step up in clutch moments, and his understanding of what it takes to navigate a long season make his arrival an invaluable asset for the Sixers. At 41, LeBron is changing teams but his ambition remains undiminished: he wants the ring.

James Harden: 'The Beard' continues to be a major asset

James Harden remains one of the NBA's top playmakers. Last season, he split his time between the Clippers and Cleveland , and after joining the Cavaliers, he averaged 20.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 7.7 assists in 26 games, quickly becoming the team’s primary offensive playmaker alongside Donovan Mitchell . His ability to control the pace, create scoring opportunities with the ball, and find his teammates remains one of his greatest strengths.

The new season finds him already a fully integrated part of the Cleveland roster, playing a central role on a team that reached the Eastern Conference Finals last season. Harden and Mitchell will now have an entire season to develop their chemistry, while the Cavaliers have also retained Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen and added new players. At 37, 'The Beard' embodies experience, creativity, and the ability to take control of games: the veteran who must put his talent to work for a team aiming to return to the ranks of the Eastern Conference’s elite.

Stephen Curry: the man who changed the NBA

Stephen Curry isn't just one of the NBA's biggest stars—he's one of the players who has most transformed the way we understand modern basketball. His revolution in three-point shooting changed defenses, opened up the court, and made long-range shots the centerpiece of many offensive plays. With four championship rings and two MVP awards, his legacy is already among the most significant of the modern era. And, at 38, he remains the Warriors ’ guiding light. Last season, he averaged 26.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 4.7 assists, which explains why he continues to be the cornerstone of his team’s identity and aspirations.

But his influence extends far beyond his shooting. For years, Curry has demonstrated an extraordinary ability to create opportunities without having the ball, constantly moving and forcing defenses to make decisions far from the basket. He continues to pose a threat capable of changing the course of a game in a matter of minutes. Some stars dominate an era; Curry helped change it. That’s why his legacy extends beyond the Warriors and he has become one of the league’s greatest icons.

Joel Embiid: a giant with limitless potential

Joel Embiid has built his superstar status on a unique profile: a 2.13-meter center capable of combining physical power, post play, outside shooting, and playmaking. His offensive dominance led him to win the 2023 MVP award and has for years made him one of the toughest players to defend in the NBA. Last season, he once again demonstrated his offensive prowess with 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, and 3.9 assists per game. When he’s on the court, Philadelphia plays a whole different game.

The big question mark has been, precisely, his availability. Injuries have shaped various stages of his career and limited his availability at decisive moments. Even so, his competitive ceiling remains unquestionable: few big men can score with such a wide variety of moves while also protecting the basket and dominating the boards. He is the giant around whom Philadelphia has built its current team and one of the faces that exemplify the power of star players in today’s NBA.

Stephen Curry isn't just one of the NBA's biggest stars—he's one of the players who has most transformed the way we understand modern basketball. His revolution in three-point shooting changed defenses, opened up the court, and made long-range shots the centerpiece of many offensive plays. With four championship rings and two MVP awards, his legacy is already among the most significant of the modern era. And, at 38, he remains the Warriors ’ guiding light. Last season, he averaged 26.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 4.7 assists, which explains why he continues to be the cornerstone of his team’s identity and aspirations.

But his influence extends far beyond his shooting. For years, Curry has demonstrated an extraordinary ability to create opportunities without having the ball, constantly moving and forcing defenses to make decisions far from the basket. He continues to pose a threat capable of changing the course of a game in a matter of minutes. Some stars dominate an era; Curry helped change it. That’s why his legacy extends beyond the Warriors and he has become one of the league’s greatest icons.
Joel Embiid: a giant with limitless potential

Joel Embiid has built his superstar status on a unique profile: a 2.13-meter center capable of combining physical power, post play, outside shooting, and playmaking. His offensive dominance led him to win the 2023 MVP award and has for years made him one of the toughest players to defend in the NBA. Last season, he once again demonstrated his offensive prowess with 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, and 3.9 assists per game. When he’s on the court, Philadelphia plays a whole different game.

The big question mark has been, precisely, his availability. Injuries have shaped various stages of his career and limited his availability at decisive moments. Even so, his competitive ceiling remains unquestionable: few big men can score with such a wide variety of moves while also protecting the basket and dominating the boards. He is the giant around whom Philadelphia has built its current team and one of the faces that exemplify the power of star players in today’s NBA.

articles.title: Knicks open NBA season with a chance to end the league’s longest drought without a repeat champion
articles.standfirst: There have been eight different champions in the last eight seasons, which is the longest streak in NBA history
articles.summary: There have been eight different champions in the last eight seasons, which is the longest streak in NBA history
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season tips off today with a high-powered three-game slate featuring the five consensus title favorites heading into the campaign.

Opening-day action begins in an innovative early time slot at 3:00 PM ET as the Boston Celtics , holding the fifth-best championship odds, visit the Detroit Pistons , who earned the top seed in the Eastern Conference last year, in a game designed to capture European primetime audiences.

Following that matchup, the New York Knicks will raise their championship banner and receive their rings at Madison Square Garden before hosting a revamped Philadelphia 76ers squad boasting the superstar tandem of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown .

The opening slate concludes in the West with a marquee Western Conference Finals rematch between the Oklahoma City Thunder and the San Antonio Spurs , two powerhouses currently sitting as the overall betting favorites to hoist the Larry O'Brien Trophy ahead of both Eastern contenders.

Knicks Seek to End Historic Era of NBA Parity

By capturing their first title in 53 seasons , New York extended a remarkable stretch that has seen eight different champions across the last eight years (Raptors, Lakers, Bucks, Warriors, Nuggets, Celtics, Thunder, and Knicks) , the longest streak of non-repeating champions in NBA history.

Across this historic era of parity, only the Golden State Warriors , Boston Celtics , and Miami Heat have managed to reach multiple Finals appearances, with Miami dropping both of their title trips.

Entering this campaign with largely the same core roster intact, the Knicks possess the continuity needed to halt this championship carousel and become the league's first back-to-back champions since the Warriors (2017–2018) .

However, across an grueling 82-game regular season where injuries and roster fluctuations dictate momentum, the true title hierarchy usually crystallizes after the 2027 All-Star Game in Phoenix .

Standing in New York's path are formidable obstacles across both conferences. In the East, the rival Philadelphia 76ers join the Knicks as co-favorites to reach the Eastern Conference Finals. Meanwhile, the Western Conference features the ultimate title favorites: the 2024-25 champion Oklahoma City Thunder and the runner-up San Antonio Spurs.

Despite displaying early postseason growing pains last spring, San Antonio enters the year with immense expectations as reigning Defensive Player of the Year Victor Wembanyama enters his fourth NBA season with valuable playoff mileage under his belt.

As opening night unfolds, the league embarks on another chapter expected to deliver iconic individual milestones, much like Bam Adebayo's historic 83-point explosion last season, and high-stakes postseason drama.
